title: The DOM Tree
summary: Elements, nodes, querySelector, textContent and safely building HTML.

steps.title: A page is a tree
body: The browser parses HTML into the **DOM** (Document Object Model): a tree of objects your JavaScript can read and change.
Every element has a parent, children, attributes (`id`, `class`, ...) and text. Changing the tree changes the page immediately.

The exercises in this module run in Node, which has no `document`, so the code steps test the **pure functions** a page relies on: turning data into HTML, validating input, deciding what to do with an event.

steps.title: Selecting and changing elements
body: const title = document.querySelector("#title");          // first match, or null
const li = document.createElement("li");                 // build a new element

`querySelector` takes **CSS selectors**: `#id`, `.class`, `tag`, `parent child`, `[data-id="2"]`. In TypeScript it returns `Element | null`, so you check for `null` (or use `querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("#name")` to get a specific element type).

> **Try it:** open the **Playground**, choose the **HTML/CSS/JS** tab and paste the HTML and script from this card. The live preview runs it in a real browser frame, and the **Tailwind** switch lets you style it with utility classes.

steps.prompt: Match each selector to what it finds.

steps.title: textContent versus innerHTML
body: `el.textContent = s` shows `s` as **text**. `el.innerHTML = s` parses `s` as **HTML**. If `s` came from a user, `innerHTML` lets them inject markup and scripts:
el.textContent = name;   // shows the characters literally: safe
el.innerHTML = name;     // runs the attacker's script: cross-site scripting (XSS)

When you build HTML strings (templates, server rendering), **escape** user data first: `&` to `&`, `<` to `<`, `>` to `>`, `"` to `"`, `'` to `'`. React and Next.js escape for you automatically, which is one big reason to use them.

steps.prompt: Safe or unsafe with untrusted text `s`?

steps.title: Escape HTML
prompt: Write `escapeHtml(s: string): string` that replaces `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'` with `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'`.
Replace `&` **first**, or you will double-escape the others.
template: Dojo.eq("tags and quotes", '<a href="x">Tom & Jerry</a>', escapeHtml('Tom & Jerry'));

steps.title: Render a list to HTML
prompt: Write `renderTasks(tasks)` returning an HTML string for a list, using your `escapeHtml`:
renderTasks([{ id: 1, title: "Write", done: true }, { id: 2, title: "<Test>", done: false }])

An empty list returns `

No tasks

`.
starter: type Task = { id: number; title: string; done: boolean };
solution: type Task = { id: number; title: string; done: boolean };
template:
Dojo.eq("two tasks", '
  • Write
  • <Test>
', renderTasks([{ id: 1, title: "Write", done: true }, { id: 2, title: "", done: false }]));
